subject: Approval request: Northridge private deployment — audit carveout & data residency asks
messages:
From: James Holloway <procurement@northridgehealth.org>

Cc: it-lead@northridgehealth.org
Date: Wed, 26 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Statement of Work + deployment model questions

Alex —

Thanks for the updated SOW. Two things on our side that are non-negotiable for a Private deployment: 1) data residency — all customer data and backups must remain in our VPC in us-east-1 (no egress outside the account), and 2) audit & inspection rights — we need the ability to perform an onsite or remote audit of the runtime and logs at least once per year with 30 days' notice.

We also flagged telemetry and diagnostics in the contract; we need explicit language that no customer PII will be sent to Redwood telemetry systems without prior written consent.

Attaching the audit scope outline and redlines. Please escalate for approvals on your side — these are deal breakers for our compliance team.

Regards,
James Holloway
Head of Procurement, Northridge Health

Forwarding Northridge's asks — their procurement is pushing hard on data-residency-in-VPC and a right to audit (onsite/remote once per year). They also want a clause preventing any PII telemetry without consent. Attached are their scope and our current SOW.

Why I'm escalating: their audit request as written gives them broad access (runtime, logs, personnel interviews) and no constraints on frequency or third-party auditors. Legal is concerned. They are also asking for absolute residency inside their VPC which we can do technically, but it changes our support/incident processes and may require a private deployment SKU.

Proposed trade: we can accept a scoped audit (defined windows, narrow log subsets, 2-week notice for onsite, Redwood personnel present) + a 10% concession on list pricing for a 12-month committed term. Need leadership signoff on the audit carveout and discount cap.

Please reply with firm approvals or suggested alternate guardrails — we need to respond to Northridge by Friday EOD.

— Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Northridge_SOW_v2.pdf

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Fwd: RE: Statement of Work + deployment model questions

Alex — thanks for the flag and the docs. I reviewed their redlines. Summary of legal concerns:

- "Audit rights" as written are too broad: they request access to runtime internals, arbitrary personnel interviews, and unlimited third-party auditors.
- "No egress" language for backups & logs inside their account is acceptable technically but we need a clause that still allows Redwood to run monitoring agents for safety & support, and a carveout for incident response that can cross-account with explicit notice.
- Telemetry/PII: we should add explicit opt-in language and a technical appendix describing what telemetry is collected by default and how to disable it.

My recommended compromise (to present to Northridge):
1) Audit: one remote audit per 12 months + optional onsite once in the first contract year with 30 days' notice; audits are scope-limited to configuration, access controls, and archival procedures — no arbitrary runtime interrogation. Third-party auditors allowed only if pre-approved by Redwood and limited to approved scope.
2) Residency: accept VPC-only deployment with the caveat that Redwood will maintain limited support connectivity (mutual TLS) for incident response; any cross-account access requires a legal hold and 7-day notice.
3) Telemetry: include an appendix and opt-in for advanced telemetry; all telemetry pipelines must be scrubbed of PII by default.

Business ask: if we accept those concessions, recommend approving a one-time 12% commercial concession (discount) and require a minimum 12-month commitment + accelerated support add-on. If leadership won't permit 12%, we can cap at 10% and add a customer-funded SOC2 readiness assessment as a compromise.

I'm seeking leadership approval on the audit carveouts and the discount cap.

— Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 14:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: RE: Statement of Work + deployment model questions

Thanks for the thoughtful notes. I reviewed the proposed compromise and approve moving forward on the following narrow exception path for Northridge Health:

1) Residency: approve VPC-only private deployment in us-east-1 with the standard support connectivity (mutual TLS) and a documented incident-response cross-account process.
2) Audit: approve one remote audit per 12 months scoped to access controls, configuration, and archival procedures. Allow one onsite audit in the first 12 months limited to the same scope. Third-party auditors permitted only with prior written approval and NDA; customer must cover reasonable travel and logistics costs. Any onsite requests require 30 days' notice and Redwood personnel present.
3) Telemetry: accept opt-in advanced telemetry with PII redaction by default; require customer sign-off prior to enabling.
4) Commercial: approve up to a 10% one-time concession on list pricing for a 12-month committed term. Any discount >10% requires VP-level signoff. Include a clause that Norton (sic) — corrected: Northridge — covers costs for additional compliance work (e.g., customer-funded SOC2 readiness assessment) if requested.

Next steps: Alex — respond to James with the carveout language (legal will send redline) and include the DocuSign link for a 12-month term at the agreed concession. Marcus, Laura — I'll follow up if there is any material deviation.

Rishi Malhotra
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
